notes.text: Listen — God turns his speech to the Gentiles, and invites them to hearken to those counsels and doctrines which the Jews would reject. Me - Unto Christ: Isaiah speaks these words in the name of Christ.

A sword — As he made me the great teacher of his church, so he made my word, quick and powerful, and sharper than any two- edged sword. Hath he hid - He will protect me from all mine enemies. Made me - Like an arrow, whose point is bright and polished; which therefore pierceth deeper.

O Israel — As the name of David is sometimes given to his successors, so here the name of Israel may not unfitly be given to Christ, not only because he descended from his loins; but also because he was the true and the great Israel, who, in a more eminent manner, prevailed with God, as that name signifies, of whom Jacob, who was first called Israel, was but a type.

Then said I — Lord, thou sayest thou wilt be glorified by my ministry; but I find it otherwise. In vain - Without any considerable fruit of my word and works among the Israelites. My judgment - My right, the reward which by his promise, and my purchase, is my right.

To bring — To convert the apostate Israelites to God. Not gathered - Not brought home to God by my ministry. Yet - God will not despise me for the unsuccessfulness of my labours, but will honour and glorify me. My strength - To support and strengthen me under this and all other discouragements.

He — The Lord. It is - This is but a small favour. The tribes - That remnant of them which shall survive all their calamities. My salvation - The great instrument and author of that eternal salvation which I will give to the Gentiles.

His Holy One — The Holy One of Israel. To him - To Christ, to whom, in the days of his flesh, this description fully agrees: for men, both Jews and Gentiles among whom he lived, did despise him from their hearts; and the nation, of which he was a member, abhorred both his person and his doctrine; and he was so far from being a temporal monarch, that he came in the form of a servant, and was a servant of rulers, professing subjection and paying tribute unto Caesar. Kings - Though for a time thou shalt be despised, yet after a while thou shalt be advanced to such glory, that kings shall look upon thee with reverence. Arise - From their seats to worship thee. Faithful - Because God shall make good his promises to thee. Chuse thee - And although thou shalt be rejected by thine own people, yet God will manifest to the world, that thou, and thou only, art the person whom he hath chosen to be the Redeemer of mankind.

glossa.text: *Hear, ye islands.* ((HIER.)) After the calling of the remnant of Israel and the objection of the unbelieving (concerning whom, *There is no peace to the wicked, saith the Lord* ), under the name of the islands he addresses, in the person of the Son, the Churches from among the Gentiles.
*A sharp sword. I came not to send peace, but the sword ((Matth. X))*, separating, that is, the evil from the good.
*I will be glorified.* Which he was not in the other servants: *Father, I have glorified thy name ((Joan. XVII.))* And elsewhere: *Arise, my glory ((Psal. LVI))*, etc.

*And I said.* ((ID.)) As though he said: How have I glorified thee, I who could not call back to thee a great part of the Jews? But here man's free choice is shown: for it is God's to call, ours to believe, yet with him helping, that the just may obtain the reward of their will.

*Therefore my judgment,* etc. ((ID.)) The Father shall judge whether I have done for them all the things I owed: *I have manifested thy name to the men whom thou gavest me.* And elsewhere: *I have glorified thee upon the earth ((Joan. XVII))*.

*My work.* Others: My labour and my sorrow: because he wept over the city, and said in the Psalm: *What profit is there in my blood? ((Psal. XXIX.))* According to the Hebrew, hanging on the cross far from my salvation are the words of my lamentations.
*Glorified.* As though he said: I have lost the Jews, but I am glorified among the Gentiles, whence, *All power is given to me in heaven and in earth. ((Matth. XXVIII))*.

*Abhorred.* Christ and his Nazarenes, whom the Jews daily curse in their synagogues, because on their account they lost their kingdom, their place and their nation.

*Kings.* The prophet to the Son. *Kings shall see* thee coming to judgment: *Kings,* namely the apostles and the others who shall judge with the Lord.

notes.text: Pit — Desperate dangers and calamities. Rock - A place of strength and safety. Established - Kept me from falling into mischief.
And fear — Shall stand in awe of that God, whom they see to have so great power, either to save or to destroy.

The proud — Or, the mighty, the great and proud potentates of the world, to whom most men are apt to look and trust. Turn - From God, in whom alone they ought to trust. To lies - To lying vanities, such as worldly power and wisdom, and riches, and all other earthly things, or persons, in which men are prone to trust: which are called lies, because they promise more than they perform.
Many — This verse seems to be interposed as a wall of partition, between that which David speaks in his own person, and that which he speaks in the person of the Messiah, in the following verses.

Sacrifice — These and the following words, may in an improper sense belong to the time of David; when God might be said, not to desire or require legal sacrifices comparatively. Thou didst desire obedience rather than sacrifices, but in a proper sense, they belong only to the person and times of the Messiah, and so the sense is, God did not desire or require them, for the satisfaction of his own justice, and the expiation of mens sins, which could not possibly be done by the blood of bulls or goats, but only by the blood of Christ, which was typified by them, and which Christ came into the world to shed, in pursuance of his father's will, as it here follows, ver. 7, 8. So here is a prediction concerning the cessation of the legal sacrifice, and the substitution of a better instead of them. Opened - Hebrew. bored. I have devoted myself to thy perpetual service, and thou hast accepted of me as such, and signified so much by the boring of mine ears, according to the law and custom in that case, Exod. xxi, 5, 6. The seventy Jewish interpreters, whom the apostle follows, Heb. x, 5, translate these words, a body hast thou prepared me.

Them — These words literally and truly belong to Christ, and the sense is this; seeing thou requirest a better sacrifice than those of the law, lo, I offer myself to come, and I will in due time come, into the world, as this phrase is explained in divers places of scripture, and particularly Heb. x, 5, where this place is expressly applied to Christ. Volume - These two words, volume and book are used of any writing, and both express the same thing. Now this volume of the book is the law of Moses, which is commonly and emphatically called the book, and was made up in the form of a roll or volume, as the Hebrew books generally were. And so this place manifestly points to Christ, concerning whom much is said in the books of Moses.

I delight — This is eminently true, of Christ, and is here observed as an act of heroic obedience, that he not only resolved to do, but delighted in doing the will of God, or what God had commanded him, which was to die, and that a most shameful, and painful, and cursed death. My heart - I do not only understand it, but receive it with heartiest love, delighting both to meditate of it, and to yield obedience to it.

Righteousness — Thy faithfulness. Great congregation - In the most public and solemn assemblies: not only to the Jews, but also to all nations; to whom Christ preached by his apostles, as is observed Eph. ii, 17. Not refrained - From preaching it, even to the face of mine enemies.

With-hold not — David, having been transported by the spirit of God to the commemoration of the great mystery of the Messiah, he now seems to be led back by the same spirit, to the consideration of his own case.

glossa.text:
*Waiting I have waited.* ((ID.)) He waits, and is ungrateful: but waiting he waits. ((AUG.)) Authority from the ancients, in Abraham and the rest, etc., *as far as* who is ours by worship, not of others.

*The Lord.* ((ID.)) Not a man, who can deceive and be deceived, and who is in need together with me. *He gave heed.* ((ID.)) To me, that he might profit me: not me, as the wicked also.

*The pit.* ((ID.)) The darkness of iniquities, that is, of unbelief and of ignorance, etc., *as far as: to a rock* against mire. ((HIER.)) But in *the pit* and in *the mire,* the Gentiles worshipping idols: or, all who love earthly things.

*A song.* ((HIER.)) Not a shameful one, not a theatrical one, but through the New Testament. *They shall see.* ((CASS.)) The wonders wrought in the time of the incarnation. ((AUG.)) They shall see: this which he first said of those before, many later peoples shall see.

*A name.* ((ID.)) Which is Saviour. As if: *Blessed,* etc., who hopes not for temporal things from him, but for salvation, which his name indicates. In the Hebrew genitives are often doubled in this manner: or, *blessed* is he to whom the name belongs, that is, by whom is the praise of God, that from him alone he may believe salvation to be, whence also is his hope. *Madnesses.* ((CASS.)) Idols, which deceive away from the truth: or, madnesses, in deceitful spectacles. Therefore in the plural, that it may be taken of them all. These things are false, but thy wonderful works, heaven, earth, dashes superstitions to pieces.

*Thy wonders.* ((AUG.)) Peter walking upon the waters in a sign, not in the world, that is, in the fruits of the world. ((AUG.)) Salvation is truthful, madness lying; it is not what it is thought to be. ((HIER.)) Earthly things are vain, madnesses, angers and brawls, etc.

*There is none like unto thee.* ((AUG.)) No authors of the arts. *I have declared.* Here Christ in the head and in the members. These are the wonders of God, these the thoughts to which no one is like. ((CASS.)) Behold the wonders: the incarnation, the justice of preaching, the deliverance of men from iniquities, the confounding of enemies, the gladness of those who hope. First, the rude and unformed were prepared, that they might willingly receive the words of Christ. ((AUG.)) See the wonders of God. I declared beforehand through the Prophets, and afterward I myself spoke. *They are multiplied in number.* ((HIER., AUG.)) Above the number of those to be saved: or, above what anyone could count: or, while I speak, more have believed than of old.

*Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire.* ((AUG.)) When the thing came, he did not want, as it were, the words that promise, etc., *as far as* but he who poured it out, being deaf, hears not. *But ears thou hast perfected for me.* That is, thou hast made me perfectly understand what thou wouldst. *Or, a body thou hast fitted to me,* as the Apostle says to the Hebrews ((Heb. X)), that is, thou hast given me a body fit for offering.

*A holocaust.* Holocausts also thou didst not require for sin. *For sin.* Which stands above *oblation,* as concerning the goat ἀποπομπάιῳ, that is, the emissary, which was sent into the desert with the sins of the people: or, for sin may be two words. *Behold I come* ((CASS.)) Since the sacrifices cease, it is established that Christ comes.

*In the head of the book it is written of me.* Behold, I come at once to do thy will, because in the head of this book. Or, it is thus predetermined with God the Father, who is my head, I who am the book, that is, the form of justice for men.

*A great church.* ((AUG.)) In the whole round of the lands, not a small one as before: and if indeed fear shall rise up, it will not forbid speaking. *Lord, thou hast known.* ((ID.)) Lips sound to men, etc., *as far as* that I be not slothful unto this.
*I have not hidden.* ((CASS.)) (When I could profit) the truth, the promise, and the salvation.
*Thy mercy.* ((AUG.)) Love and fear lead me through unto thee.

notes.text: An exhortation to concord, beating down all glorying in the flesh, 4- iv.21

A reproof,

1. For not excommunicating the incestuous person, v. 1-13

2. For going to law before heathen Judges, vi. 1-11

3. A dissuasive from fornication, 12-20

4. An answer to the questions they had proposed concerning marriage, vii. 1, 10, 25, 36, 39

5. Concerning things sacrificed to idols, viii. 1- ix. 1

6. Concerning the veiling of women, 2-16

7. Concerning the Lord's supper, 17-34

8. Concerning spiritual gifts, xii. xiii. xiv

9. Concerning the resurrection, xv. 1-58

10. Concerning the collection for the poor, the coming of himself, of Timothy, of Apollos, the sum of all, xvi, 1, 5, 10, 12, 13, 14 II. The conclusion, 15, 17, 19-24 1st CORINTHIANS
Always — Whenever I mention you to God in prayer.

In all utterance and knowledge — Of divine things. These gifts the Corinthians particularly admired. Therefore this congratulation naturally tended to soften their spirits, and I make way for the reproofs which follow.

The testimony of Christ — The gospel. Was confirmed among you - By these gifts attending it. They knew they had received these by the hand of Paul: and this consideration was highly proper, to revive in them their former reverence and affection for their spiritual father.
Waiting — With earnest desire. For the glorious Revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ - A sure mark of a true or false Christian, to long for, or dread, this Revelation.

Who will also — if you faithfully apply to him. Confirm you to the end. In the day of Christ - Now it is our day, wherein we are to work out our salvation; then it will be eminently the day of Christ, and of his glory in the saints.
God is faithful — To all his promises; and therefore "to him that hath shall be given." By whom ye are called - A pledge of his willingness to save you unto the uttermost.

glossa.text: *Paul, called.* That is, named by all with the privilege of the name, *an apostle of Jesus Christ.* Here he does not name himself a servant: because there was rather need of authority and of commendation against the pride of the Corinthians, in whose eyes he had grown cheap. *And Sosthenes.* Behold, he hints that it was through him who was living among them that he had learned their faults. *A brother.* By this he removes it, that he had made it known to him not out of an evil mind, but out of charity and a desire of correction.
*With all.* And he writes to all the suffragan Corinthians, who laboured under the same vices.

*Grace.* First he sets forth what belongs to the good, that others may be conformed to these. *And from the Lord Jesus Christ.* Who is indeed distinguished from the Father by a personal property, but is one God with him by unity of substance.
*In all things.* He subjoins certain particulars, in every word, that is, in every kind of tongues, or in every manner of preaching, that is, to the lesser, the middling, and the perfect.

notes.text: He seeth Jesus coming and saith, Behold the Lamb — Innocent; to be offered up; prophesied of by Isaiah, Isaiah liii, 7, typified by the paschal lamb, and by the daily sacrifice: The Lamb of God - Whom God gave, approves, accepts of; who taketh away - Atoneth for; the sin - That is, all the sins: of the world - Of all mankind. Sin and the world are of equal extent.

I knew him not — Till he came to be baptized. How surprising is this; considering how nearly they were related, and how remarkable the conception and birth of both had been. But there was a peculiar providence visible in our saviour's living, from his infancy to his baptism, at Nazareth: John all the time living the life of a hermit in the deserts of Judea, Luke i, 80, ninety or more miles from Nazareth: hereby that acquaintance was prevented which might have made John's testimony of Christ suspected.
I saw it — That is, the Spirit so descending and abiding on him. And testified - From that time.
They followed Jesus — They walked after him, but had not the courage to speak to him.

He first findeth his own brother Simon — Probably both of them sought him: Which is, being interpreted, the Christ - This the evangelist adds, as likewise those words in ver. 38, that is, being interpreted, Master.

Jesus said, Thou art Simon, the son of Jonah — As none had told our Lord these names, this could not but strike Peter. Cephas, which is Peter - Moaning the same in Syriac which Peter does in Greek, namely, a rock.

glossa.text: *The next day John saw Jesus.* Typically. John, that is, the people of grace, on the next day, that is, after the law, knows the lamb by whom it is redeemed. *Coming to him, and he says.* Not only by the steps of the body, but also by the approaches of his own inward contemplation, because he deigned to be known by John according to his divinity and his humanity. *Behold the Lamb of God,* etc. Three things the lamb supplies to those who possess him: the milk of simple doctrine, by which little ones are nourished; the wool, that is, the increases of the virtues; the eating of his flesh. *The sins of the world.* The sin of the world is called original sin, which is common to the whole world, by which the whole of human nature, founded at once and together, transgressed the divine laws through disobedience in paradise; and that original sin, and the several sins added on top of it, grace looses.
*After me there comes a man.* Christ is man, in which he agrees with us and pays on our behalf; and Son of God, in which he agrees with the Father, and by forgiving sins reconciles us to him.

*That he may be made manifest.* This is the lamb who takes away sins, which I am not, whom also I now know better; but for this reason do I baptize, that he may be made manifest to Israel. For lest, on account of the strangeness of it, they should be the less baptized by Christ in the Spirit, he prepared the way for him by the practice of baptizing; whence, after men had come to him who is the way, his baptism ceases. In John's baptism also the humility of Christ is made manifest, which is the fulfilling of all justice; for as it was needful that Christ should be born and die, so also that he should be baptized. For if he himself, who has no need, is baptized by a servant, let not men, however wise and holy, disdain to be baptized by the Lord, without whom they remain in their sins. *Baptizing.* Christ is baptized by John, that all humility, which is all justice, may be shown. But not he alone, lest the baptism of John, in which God-and-man was baptized, should seem holier and greater than the baptism of Christ, in which men are baptized. But others are baptized by John, so that the practice of baptizing may prepare the way for the baptism of Christ.

*And testimony.* As he said that he had come to make Christ manifest, so he bore testimony, namely: *he saw the Spirit.* In which he learned what he did not know before. He had come also to preach penance, that is, to make the preparation for Christ's preaching; but he sets down only the preparation of baptism by itself, because the baptism of Christ is the highest sacrament among the rest. *The Spirit descending.* Not that he then first descended, but that by this he might be shown to descend and to remain in those baptized in water and not otherwise, and that John through him might understand more excellently concerning Christ.

*And I knew him not. ((AUG.))* The dove having been seen, he says that through it he learned what he did not know before, etc., *as far as* whence the Apostle: *In labour and in mind they are different, in working undifferentiated.*

((HIER.)) He shows that John did not know, by the baptism of Christ, that is, that the world was redeemed; for he knew him to be the Son of God and born in the flesh. Aug. says that John was ignorant of this only: whether he would keep to himself the power of baptizing, or would grant it to some one of his own. *And remaining. ((AUG.))* Spiritually the Spirit is said to remain in Christ, from whom he never withdrew through sin, in whom he always lived wonderfully and wonderfully wrought; into the saints he comes, and through sins he withdraws. Yet he always remains in them for something, as Christ promised them, namely, that they may always press on in good things. For something he does not remain, namely, that they should prophesy from him or work miracles; and therefore this which he says is the first sign of recognizing Christ.

*Who baptizes.* Christ baptizes in the Spirit, not only by remitting sins in the water, but also by cleansing afterwards, and by kindling love, and by filling with gifts.

 *This is the Son of God.* Here he testifies him to be the Son of God whom above he was calling a man: so that from him there may be had a testimony of either nature.
*The next day John was standing again.* Typically. John stands, the law ceases, yet bearing testimony to Christ. Jesus walks, that is, grace, gathering from this side and from that.

*They followed Jesus.* They followed, that they might now hear him rather than John, not yet however cleaving to him wholly, but that they might see where he dwells, that they might come to him constantly and be taught by him; and afterwards they followed perfectly, when he called them from the boat. Two follow, because they who follow ought to be kindled with a twofold charity.

*Turning.* As it were from behind they had seen him, but as it were he offered them his face when he came down from his majesty, that he might be able to be seen, when in place of the shadow of the law he showed forth the light of the Gospel. *What seek ye?* He asks, not as one ignorant, but that they who answer may have a reward: he asks the thing, not the person, *what*, not *whom*, lest he should seem to show himself; they answer the person. *Where dwellest thou?* Mystically. They wish it to be shown them in whom Christ dwells, that they may make themselves like to them. Or: they who see the incarnation devoutly ask that it be shown them how the eternal dwelling is with the Father.

*Come.* As if to say: it cannot be unfolded in speech, but is shown in work; come by believing and by working, and you shall understand; come by the testimony of John, and withdraw from the law, and you shall receive grace. *That day.* He shows the New Testament, or the present life. *And it was about the tenth hour.* Because they had come from the law, the decalogue sent them to Christ; at the tenth hour they seek to be taught by him, because none other teaches the law but he who gave it. And he teaches with mercy, and those things are fulfilled which they could not fulfil; or the tenth hour indicates the evening of the world.

*The brother of Simon Peter, one of the two who had heard from John, and had followed.* The brother younger in birth believes first, for the order of faith is not an empty thing. Perhaps for dignity Andrew is said to be the brother of Peter, upon whom, that is, upon whose faith, the Church was to be founded.

*He findeth first.* True piety at once announces the treasure it has found to its brother, that as he is a brother by blood, so he may be a brother also in faith. *We have found the Messias,* etc. Christus in Greek, Messias in Hebrew, anointed in Latin: for he was truly and in a special way anointed by the Holy Spirit, and from that anointing Christians are named. That Jacob, after the vision, set up a stone for a pillar which the pouring on of oil anointed: already by divine gift he figuratively understood, through that rock, the rock to come, namely Christ, who was to be anointed with the Holy Spirit; and he prefigured that the Church was so to be founded upon that rock, etc.

*Thou art Simon the son.* First he says the name as he has it from his parents, that the change may be signified when from Simon he calls him Peter. But in the change is marked the liveliness of the mystery; yet neither is the former name without power. For Simon is *obedient*, son of grace or of the dove, when he comes to Jesus, following his brother; whence from the rock, that is Christ, he is called Peter, weak in him, in the figure of the Church which is founded upon the rock.

*Thou art Simon. ((CHRYS.))* He changed the name for this reason, that he might show that it is he himself who gave the Old Testament and changed names: because he called Abram Abraham, and Sarai Sara, and Jacob Israel. Therefore upon many he laid names even from their birth, as upon Isaac and Samson; but upon others after the naming which comes from their forebears, as upon Peter and the sons of Zebedee. For those in whom virtue was to shine out from their first age received their names from that time; but those in whom it was afterwards to be increased, upon them the naming was set afterwards.

*Son of Joanna,* etc. Jona and Joanna are said indifferently. Jona is interpreted *dove,* Joanna *grace.*

echoes.text: It will happen that whoever will call on Yahweh’s name shall be saved; for in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, as Yahweh has said, and among the remnant, those whom Yahweh calls.
echoes.note: 'All who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place' reworks Joel's 'everyone who calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved,' transferring the divine Name to Jesus. Volume is high (distinctive idiom 'call on the name'), recurrence strong in Paul (Rom 10:13), and the eschatological-salvation theme coheres tightly with the surrounding 'day of the Lord' language.

echoes.text: and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel.”
echoes.note: The address to those 'sanctified... called to be saints' transfers Israel's vocation as a 'holy nation' set apart for God to the Corinthian assembly. The lexical pairing of calling and holiness coheres thematically with the Sinai constitution of a consecrated people; the volume is modest because Paul cites no formula, but the figural availability of Exodus 19 to a Jewish reader is high.

echoes.text: For I am Yahweh your God. Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be holy; for I am holy: neither shall you defile yourselves with any kind of creeping thing that moves on the earth. For I am Yahweh who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. You shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.
echoes.note: 'Sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints' echoes the Holiness Code refrain 'be holy, for I am holy,' in which Israel's status as God's set-apart people is grounded in God's own holiness. Recurrence is strong across Leviticus 19-20, and the thematic coherence of consecration as gift-and-summons fits Paul's idiom of being made holy in Christ.

echoes.text: It will happen, that he who is left in Zion, and he who remains in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even everyone who is written among the living in Jerusalem;
echoes.note: The phrase 'called holy' (kalein hagion) for the eschatological remnant in Zion resonates with 'called to be saints.' The verbal link is suggestive in the LXX, but the volume is faint and the motif is widely diffused, so it is offered only as a contested resonance.

echoes.text: A son was also born to Seth, and he named him Enosh. At that time men began to call on Yahweh’s name.
echoes.note: The idiom 'call on the name of the LORD' first appears at the dawn of worship in Genesis 4:26 and runs through the patriarchal narratives (Gen 12:8; 13:4). It supplies the deep semantic background for Paul's phrase, though Joel is the proximate and more specific source.

echoes.text: I will take the cup of salvation, and call on Yahweh’s name.
echoes.note: The cultic act of 'calling on the name of the LORD' in the thanksgiving psalter underlies the worship-language of 'all who call on the name.' Recurrence within the Psalms is notable, but the volume here is faint relative to the Joel allusion that controls the phrase.

echoes.text: For then I will purify the lips of the peoples, that they may all call on Yahweh’s name, to serve him shoulder to shoulder.
echoes.note: Zephaniah's promise that the nations will 'call on the name of the LORD' with one accord matches Paul's universalizing 'in every place, both theirs and ours.' The thematic coherence of an ingathered people invoking the Name is good, but the verbal contact is light and the motif overlaps with Joel.

echoes.text: “Woe to you who desire the day of Yahweh! Why do you long for the day of Yahweh? It is darkness, and not light.
echoes.note: The repeated 'day of our Lord Jesus Christ' (v.8) draws on the prophetic 'day of the LORD' tradition, of which Amos is the classic warning text. Thematic coherence is strong: Paul reframes the eschatological day as the point of vindication 'blameless,' and the recurrence of yom YHWH across the prophets gives the motif high availability.

echoes.text: The sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of Yahweh comes.
echoes.note: 'The day of our Lord' as the eschatological revelation aligns with Joel's 'great and terrible day of the LORD,' the same chapter Paul has just drawn on in v.2. The internal recurrence (Joel within the immediate context) strengthens the case for a Joel-shaped horizon, though the phrase is generic enough to be merely traditional.

echoes.text: Know therefore that Yahweh your God himself is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness with them who love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations,
echoes.note: 'God is faithful, through whom you were called' (v.9) echoes the covenant formula that 'the LORD your God is the faithful God who keeps covenant.' Volume is good on the distinctive predicate 'faithful' applied to God as the guarantor of a calling, and the covenant-keeping theme coheres with Paul's assurance of preservation to the end.

echoes.text: The great day of Yahweh is near. It is near, and hurries greatly, the voice of the day of Yahweh. The mighty man cries there bitterly.
echoes.note: Zephaniah's 'great day of the LORD is near' is among the most concentrated 'day of the LORD' oracles and feeds the same prophetic reservoir behind v.8. The volume is low because Paul names no specific feature of Zephaniah's day, but the motif's availability is high.

echoes.text: “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap;
echoes.note: 'Who can stand when he appears?'—the day that tests and refines—coheres with Paul's hope that the Corinthians be 'confirmed... blameless in the day.' The forensic-purgative coloring of being found unblamable resonates, but the connection is thematic rather than verbal.

echoes.text: The Rock, his work is perfect, for all his ways are just. A God of faithfulness who does no wrong, just and right is he.
echoes.note: The Song of Moses names God 'faithful (pistos) and without iniquity,' a likely LXX source for Paul's 'God is faithful.' Recurrence of the divine epithet pistos in Deuteronomy supports availability, though the phrase had become a settled liturgical commonplace.

echoes.text: Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying, ‘On the tenth day of this month, they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to their fathers’ houses, a lamb for a household; and if the household is too little for a lamb, then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take one according to the number of the souls; according to what everyone can eat you shall make your count for the lamb. Your lamb shall be without defect, a male a year old. You […]
echoes.note: 'Behold, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world' (v.29) reads Jesus through the Passover lamb whose blood delivers Israel. John's later Passover chronology (Jesus dying as the lambs are slain, no bones broken) confirms this figural channel. High volume and thematic coherence.

echoes.text: He was oppressed, yet when he was afflicted he didn’t open his mouth. As a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and as a sheep that before its shearers is mute, so he didn’t open his mouth.
echoes.note: The Servant 'led like a lamb to the slaughter' who bears the sin of many is the strongest source for a sin-bearing Lamb (v.29), since the Passover lamb is not explicitly sin-removing. The combination of lamb imagery with sin-bearing points decisively to the Servant Song. High coherence.

echoes.text: The Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'The Spirit of the LORD shall rest on him' undergirds the Spirit 'descending and remaining on him' (vv.32-33); the abiding (not transient) anointing marks the messianic endowment. High thematic coherence with the messianic identification that follows.

echoes.text: “Behold, my servant, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delights— I have put my Spirit on him. He will bring justice to the nations.
echoes.note: 'My chosen, on whom I have put my Spirit' fuses the Servant with the Spirit-resting/abiding motif of vv.32-34, and 'Son of God' (v.34, with a known variant 'chosen one') strengthens the Servant link. High coherence between Spirit-endowed Servant and the baptismal attestation.

echoes.text: Abraham said, “God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they both went together.
echoes.note: 'God will provide himself the lamb' (the Aqedah) supplies a God-provided sacrificial lamb that became central in Second-Temple atonement reflection, coherent with 'the Lamb of God' (the lamb God provides). Medium because the verbal link is the divine-provision phrase rather than direct quotation.

echoes.text: The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
echoes.note: The Spirit hovering over the waters at creation, evoked by the Spirit descending over the baptismal waters as a dove (v.32), ties the Spirit-baptism to a new-creation motif consonant with the Prologue's Genesis framing. Medium: the dove-over-water image is the figural cue.

echoes.text: He himself sent out a dove to see if the waters were abated from the surface of the ground, but the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned to him into the ship, for the waters were on the surface of the whole earth. He put out his hand, and took her, and brought her to him into the ship. He waited yet another seven days; and again he sent the dove out of the ship. The dove came back to him at evening and, behold, in her mouth was a freshly […]
echoes.note: Noah's dove returning over the receding flood-waters offers a dove-over-water image often linked to the baptismal dove (v.32) and to new creation after judgment. Low and contested as a deliberate source, but recurrent in early Jewish-Christian dove symbolism.

echoes.text: “Now this is that which you shall offer on the altar: two lambs a year old day by day continually. The one lamb you shall offer in the morning; and the other lamb you shall offer at evening: and with the one lamb a tenth part of an ephah of fine flour mixed with the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil, and the fourth part of a hin of wine for a drink offering. The other lamb you shall offer at evening, and shall do to it according to the meal offering of […]
echoes.note: The daily Tamid lamb offered morning and evening provides another sacrificial-lamb backdrop for 'the Lamb of God' (v.29) alongside Passover and Isaiah 53. Low confidence; included for recurrence of cultic lamb imagery available to John.

echoes.text: But I was like a gentle lamb that is led to the slaughter; and I didn’t know that they had devised devices against me, saying, Let us destroy the tree with its fruit, and let us cut him off from the land of the living, that his name may be no more remembered.
echoes.note: 'I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter' echoes the innocent-victim lamb of v.29, reinforcing the Isaiah 53 sense. Faint and contested as an independent source but a genuine OT lamb-as-victim parallel.

echoes.text: He was oppressed, yet when he was afflicted he didn’t open his mouth. As a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and as a sheep that before its shearers is mute, so he didn’t open his mouth.
echoes.note: The repeated 'Behold, the Lamb of God' (v.36) re-applies the same Servant-lamb identification, the recurrence of which (vv.29,36) strengthens the Isaiah 53 reading under Hays' recurrence criterion. Medium as it is a restatement of the v.29 source.

echoes.text: Neither will your name any more be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham; for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
echoes.note: Jesus' renaming of Simon to Cephas/Peter (v.42) follows the OT pattern of God renaming at covenant calling (Abram to Abraham). The name-change-as-vocation motif coheres with the call narrative; low because no single text is quoted.

echoes.text: He said, “Your name will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel; for you have fought with God and with men, and have prevailed.”
echoes.note: Jacob renamed Israel after the encounter at the Jabbok is a second instance of the divine-renaming pattern behind Simon to Cephas (v.42), and anticipates the Jacob/Israel motifs that culminate in v.51. Low and contested as a direct source.

harmony.title: The Baptism of Jesus
harmony.note: John's Gospel reports it obliquely, through the Baptist's testimony — "I have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God."

harmony.title: The first disciples
harmony.note: John alone gives this earlier Judean call — Andrew, Peter, Nathanael — before the Galilean one.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Behold the Lamb of God.
Who takes away the sin of the world.
He turned and asked, What are you looking for?
Teacher, where are you staying?
Come and see, he said.
And we have come to see.
Come, let us worship the One we have found.
Come and see. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: John points down the road and says it plainly: there he is, the Lamb of God — and two of them leave everything to follow.
Come and see.
Jesus turns around and looks right at them and asks the question under every question: what are you looking for?
Come and see.
They have no fine answer, only a longing — where are you staying? — and he does not lecture them; he opens his hands.
Come and see.
So whatever you came looking for this morning, bring it; the invitation is the same as it was that day.
Come and see. Thanks be to God!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Behold the Lamb of God who takes our sin.
Come and see.
He turns and asks, What are you looking for?
Come and see.
They followed him home and stayed the day.
Come and see.
Come, let us worship the One we have found.
Come and see. Thanks be to God!
